extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in Computational Linguistics, containing 73,285 papers, 210K figures, metadata, PDFs, citation graphs, and structured full texts linked to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We crawl PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages. We obtain 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages. We use GROBID for full-text extraction from PDF files. We extract figures and tables using PDFFigures. We link to Semantic Scholar Academic Graph via API.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We train a PLM-based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels. We then extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We use 5-fold cross-validation. The best performance (PLM-SPECTER) achieves 69% accuracy. We note that 13 out of 15 top-cited papers have correct predicted topics.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates. We identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Prior research found that numerous languages remain underrepresented. Even among languages in the same language group, there is a significant disparity in coverage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. It does not include other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID; some figures and tables are not detected. The corpus is unlabeled for specific tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Usage guidelines: topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, related work generation, multimodal research, knowledge graph construction, etc.
